papers.title: Hindsight Forcing: Learning Better History from the Future in Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables real-time streaming generation, with each generated chunk serving as historical context for subsequent generation. To avoid the memory explosion of backpropagation through time, previous self-rollout methods typically truncate cross-chunk gradients or detach historical latents. As a result, earlier denoising computations receive no downstream feedback through the generated history on how to synthesize frames that facilitate subsequent generation, leading to visual drift and structural collapse as rollouts extend. To address this limitation, we propose Hindsight Forcing, which allows historical chunks to learn directly from future outcomes by decoupling forward generation from backward credit assignment via a latent straight-through bridge. In the forward pass, each chunk completes a full multi-step rollout to update the KV cache. In the backward pass, the bridge routes gradients from future losses back to a single selected denoising step per historical chunk, training both the context writer and historical denoiser on shared parameters without retaining the full trajectory graph. Remarkably, Hindsight Forcing requires no additional model parameters, architecture modifications, or separate trajectory replay. Extensive experiments on VBench demonstrate that Hindsight Forcing outperforms existing baselines in overall visual quality and dynamic motion, while ablation studies validate the benefit of supervising historical denoising. Code is available at https://github.com/haonanAN309/Hindsight-Forcing.
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对少步自回归视频扩散中的长期生成退化问题，指出现有自滚动训练通常切断历史潜变量到早期去噪过程的梯度，使历史内容无法根据未来生成结果进行优化。作者提出 Hindsight Forcing：前向过程使用完整多步滚动结果构建真实推理分布下的历史 KV 缓存，反向过程则通过潜变量直通桥，将未来损失的梯度传递到每个历史块选定的去噪步骤。该方法只保留每块一个去噪图，内存开销随块数线性增长，无需额外参数、架构改动或轨迹重放。基于 Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B 的实验显示，该方法在 VBench 总分、质量和动态程度上取得较优结果，同时保持标准 KV 缓存推理流程和近似不变的推理开销。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 识别了现有自回归视频扩散蒸馏方法中的历史潜变量梯度截断问题，说明未来损失无法监督生成历史内容的早期去噪计算。2. 提出 Hindsight Forcing，利用潜变量直通桥结合完整前向滚动与选择性反向信用分配，使未来损失同时更新上下文写入过程和历史去噪过程，并共享同一组模型参数。3. 无需增加学生模型参数、修改网络架构或进行独立轨迹重放，即可在训练中实现跨块梯度传播；推理时不增加额外计算。4. 在 VBench 上进行了与多种方法的比较、组件消融和梯度传播分析，验证了监督历史去噪对视觉质量、时间一致性和动态运动的作用。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关，直接研究自回归、因果、流式和长视频生成。其方法面向实时流式视频扩散，通过 KV 缓存和少步去噪降低生成延迟，并利用未来块的损失优化历史块，使长时滚动中的结构一致性和运动连续性更稳定。潜变量直通桥属于高效的梯度信用分配与缓存复用机制，避免完整 BPTT 的高内存成本；实验中无需额外参数或推理阶段改动，适合实时生成和交互式世界模拟等场景。论文还显示，在七块训练设置下 VBench 总分达到 85.74、动态程度达到 92.22，并保持约 5.619 秒的视频推理时间。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出以下局限：第一，实验主要使用跨块和跨去噪步骤共享的固定梯度缩放因子 α；其敏感性表明，未来可探索针对不同块或去噪步骤自适应调整该因子。第二，虽然每个块仅保留一个去噪计算图，相比完整 BPTT 显著降低了激活存储，但去噪图和上下文写入图的数量仍会随滚动块数线性增长。第三，训练采用有限长度的短滚动和有界历史 KV 上下文，短滚动训练能否泛化到持续更长时间的流式生成仍需研究。实验主要基于 Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B、约五秒视频和 VBench，论文未明确说明其在更大模型、不同数据分布、更长部署时长或真实闭环交互环境中的表现。
papers.abstract_cn: 少步自回归视频扩散能够实现实时流式生成，其中每个生成的视频块都会作为后续生成的历史上下文。为避免时间反向传播带来的内存爆炸，已有自滚动方法通常会截断跨块梯度，或将历史潜变量分离。因此，较早的去噪计算无法通过生成历史获得关于如何合成有利于后续生成帧的下游反馈，导致随着滚动持续而出现视觉漂移和结构崩溃。为解决这一局限，我们提出了 Hindsight Forcing，通过潜变量直通桥将前向生成与反向信用分配解耦，使历史块能够直接从未来结果中学习。在前向传播中，每个块完成完整的多步滚动，以更新 KV 缓存；在反向传播中，该桥将来自未来损失的梯度传回每个历史块中选定的单个去噪步骤，从而在无需保留完整轨迹计算图的情况下，使用共享参数同时训练上下文写入器和历史去噪器。值得注意的是，Hindsight Forcing 不需要额外模型参数、架构修改或独立的轨迹重放。在 VBench 上的大量实验表明，Hindsight Forcing 在整体视觉质量和动态运动方面优于现有基线，而消融实验验证了监督历史去噪的益处。代码已发布于 https://github.com/haonanAN309/Hindsight-Forcing。

papers.title: ContextRenderer: Dynamic-Context Video Generation for Interactive Game Worlds
papers.abstract: Interactive game world models separate executable world evolution from visual generation, using video models to render engine-provided scene representations into detailed observations. During sustained gameplay, however, existing generative renderers struggle to follow changing conditions while preserving visual continuity across diverse proxies and target styles. We therefore introduce ContextRenderer, an autoregressive video diffusion framework designed for both dynamic conditioning and cross-proxy generalization. It couples Dynamic-Context Learning (DCL) for chunk-level interaction supervision with Recurrent History Compression (RHC) to follow condition updates while preserving visual continuity within a bounded token budget. Across proxy representations, Cross-Representation Flow Alignment (CRFA) connects proxy reconstruction with appearance and interaction variation through a shared high-fidelity reconstruction. WorldPrism, our interaction-centric dataset constructed from agent-built worlds, AAA gameplay, and open-source videos, supplies the corresponding renderings and chunk-level annotations for these learning tasks. Experiments on GWM-Bench and Solar-Bench show improved reconstruction and visual quality, while qualitative results demonstrate minute-long interactive rendering under changing prompts and subject references. Project page: https://rainzor.github.io/contextrenderer/

papers.title: SOAR: Training-Free Rank-Consistent Rollout Compression for Latent World Model Planning
papers.abstract: Latent world models plan by rolling out hundreds of candidate action sequences through a transformer predictor, so a single decision can take tens of seconds. Existing accelerations prune spatial tokens as in vision-language models, yet a sampling-based planner uses predicted costs only to rank candidates, so a rollout can be compressed freely as long as the ranking survives. We propose SOAR, a training-free method that adapts rollout compression to each planning decision. At every decision, SOAR probes a few candidates under several token budgets and keeps the smallest budget that preserves their ranking, so it compresses as far as the current decision allows, without task labels. A closed-loop study of more than 80,000 episodes fixes the rest of the rollout: the first step, which alone reads a real observation, stays exact, and the context frame is cached rather than recomputed. On seven navigation and manipulation tasks with frozen checkpoints, SOAR matches dense-level planning success at 2.3x speedup and retains 98% at 2.5x. Our code is available at https://github.com/starrywiki/SOAR.
papers.comment: 16 pages, including supplementary material. Anqi Li and Kai Liu contributed equally
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究冻结潜在世界模型中基于 CEM 的候选动作规划加速问题。作者指出，规划器只依赖候选代价的精英排序，而不要求压缩滚动保持特征或代价数值完全一致，因此应以排序一致性而非重建质量作为压缩标准。通过超过 80,000 个闭环回合，论文发现：空间标记的选择方式影响有限；读取真实观测的第一步对后续排序最关键；上下文帧对部分操作任务很重要，但可通过 KV 缓存避免重复计算。基于这些发现，SOAR 保持第一步精确、缓存上下文帧，并在每次决策中用少量候选在多个嵌套标记预算下进行探测，根据 Spearman 排名相关性选择最小可用预算。在七个导航和操作任务上，SOAR 达到稠密模型水平的规划成功率并获得 2.3 倍加速。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出面向采样式规划的排序一致性压缩准则：只要压缩滚动保留候选精英集合，规划结果即可保持不变。2. 沿空间、上下文帧、滚动步和预测器深度四个维度系统分析滚动冗余，发现计算时机比空间标记选择更重要。3. 提出 SOAR，一种无需训练、无需任务标签的在线自适应预算选择方法，用少量候选探测不同预算下的排序一致性。4. 将精确的第一步、上下文 KV 缓存和可变的新帧标记预算结合起来，在七项任务上以 2.3 倍加速达到稠密级成功率，并在 2.5 倍加速下保留 98% 的成功率。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与动作条件视觉世界模型和闭环模拟直接相关：它在 JEPA-WM 中通过 CEM 滚动生成候选动作后续状态，并用闭环任务成功率评估压缩效果。它针对自回归世界模型的长序列滚动，利用第一步精确计算、跨帧 KV 缓存和后续步骤的稀疏标记处理，降低规划延迟。其按决策动态选择计算预算的机制与实时生成、稀疏注意力和缓存复用高度相关；在冻结模型、无需蒸馏或额外训练的条件下实现了 2.3 倍规划加速。不过，论文主要研究潜在特征预测和规划滚动，而不是直接生成可观看的视频。
papers.limitations_cn: 研究使用的模型主要是具有两帧上下文的已发布 JEPA-WM 检查点，结论对更长上下文预测器的适用性仍需验证。排序一致性命题适用于仅依据候选排序选择精英的规划器，不适用于 MPPI 等代价加权规划器。SOAR 只在第一轮 CEM 候选上估计排序一致性，而后续精英候选的探测可能进一步压缩计算。论文还指出，未来可研究基于 Top-K 重叠的探测准则和更细粒度的预算集合。
papers.abstract_cn: 潜在世界模型通过变换器预测器滚动预测数百条候选动作序列，因此单次决策可能需要数十秒。现有加速方法借鉴视觉语言模型剪枝空间标记；然而，基于采样的规划器仅使用预测代价对候选项进行排序，因此只要排序保持不变，就可以自由压缩滚动过程。我们提出 SOAR，一种无需训练的方法，可针对每次规划决策自适应地压缩滚动过程。在每次决策中，SOAR 在多个标记预算下测试少量候选项，并保留能够维持候选项排序的最小预算，从而在不需要任务标签的情况下，将压缩程度推进到当前决策所允许的范围。我们对超过 80,000 个闭环回合开展研究，并固定滚动过程的其他部分：唯一读取真实观测的第一步保持精确，且上下文帧采用缓存而非重新计算。在七个导航与操作任务及冻结的模型检查点上，SOAR 以 2.3 倍加速达到与稠密级规划相当的成功率，并在 2.5 倍加速下保留 98% 的成功率。代码见 https://github.com/starrywiki/SOAR。

papers.title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement
papers.abstract: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.
papers.summary_cn: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs.
papers.contribution_cn: We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone.

papers.title: Streaming-AAA: Streaming AAA Game Video Generation at High Resolution, High Frame Rate, and Low Latency
papers.abstract: Controllable streaming video generation offers a promising route toward interactive game simulation, yet existing methods remain far from practical gameplay. They often fail to jointly achieve high visual fidelity, high frame rates, and low interaction latency, resulting in poor responsiveness and degraded user experience. We present Streaming-AAA, a new paradigm for controllable infinite generation of AAA-quality game videos. Our system generates 1080p gameplay videos at 43 FPS with 198 ms end-to-end latency interaction on merely NVIDIA A800 GPUs, while supporting long-horizon play without severe temporal degradation or collapse. Streaming-AAA is built upon three key designs. First, we redesign the VAE architecture for efficient high-resolution decoding, enabling real-time synthesis at 1080p. Second, we pretrain the diffusion model using diffusion forcing and significantly extend the temporal training horizon, allowing the model to capture long-term dependencies and maintain persistent memory. Third, we perform post-training distillation and memory compression to improve inference efficiency while retaining visual quality and temporal consistency. Experiments show that Streaming-AAA substantially improves visual fidelity, frame rate, latency, and long-term stability over prior controllable video generation approaches, enabling a significantly more playable experience for interactive AAA game video generation.
papers.summary_cn: Controllable streaming video generation offers a promising route toward interactive game simulation, yet existing methods remain far from practical gameplay.
papers.contribution_cn: We present Streaming-AAA, a new paradigm for controllable infinite generation of AAA-quality game videos.

papers.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.
papers.summary_cn: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions.

papers.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
papers.abstract: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.
papers.summary_cn: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties.

papers.title: ViewDreamer: A Robot World Model beyond Fixed Camera Setups
papers.abstract: Video generation models are increasingly important for robot learning, yet most generate each camera view separately or tile all views in a fixed layout. Robot demonstrations, however, are captured by synchronized cameras whose number, placement, and order vary across embodiments. We present ViewDreamer, a single world model that handles variable sets of cameras by disentangling per-view generation from cross-view interaction. Each view follows the generation path of a pretrained single-view model, and views interact only through shared slot tokens. We stabilize multi-view training with a curriculum that gradually increases the number of views. Cross-View Slot Agreement uses visual foundation models to group geometrically and semantically similar regions across views into shared slots. On RoboView-Bench, which covers one to four cameras, ViewDreamer achieves the best generation quality among the models evaluated and improves cross-view consistency over independent per-view generation. These gains carry over to our world-action model (WAM) and action-conditioned world model (AC-WM). Our WAM outperforms the FastWAM-Joint baseline on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboDojo, and on a real Franka robot. Both variants improve out-of-domain generalization to various camera settings and scenes.
papers.summary_cn: Video generation models are increasingly important for robot learning, yet most generate each camera view separately or tile all views in a fixed layout.
papers.contribution_cn: We present ViewDreamer, a single world model that handles variable sets of cameras by disentangling per-view generation from cross-view interaction.

papers.title: SonoAtlasWorld: Anatomy-Grounded Ultrasound World Models for Wide-Range Scanning
papers.abstract: Learning robotic ultrasound policies requires interactive environments for scalable data generation and repeatable evaluation, while exploration on real patients is limited by acquisition costs and safety constraints. Generative world models offer an alternative, but image history and probe actions alone do not ensure anatomical consistency across wide-range scans and changing acoustic windows. We introduce SonoAtlasWorld, an ultrasound world model built on anatomy as state. A persistent 3D anatomical asset extracted from computed tomography (CT) anchors each scan to a specific anatomy. Probe actions determine anatomical and acoustic visibility conditions for a causal ultrasound generator trained on clinical videos. Our three-stage pipeline combines anatomy-conditioned pretraining, causal conversion and long-rollout alignment. Inference optimizations achieve pose-to-ultrasound throughput of 81.2 FPS. To evaluate anatomical control beyond image similarity, we introduce the Action-Following Index (AFI), which measures normalized reconstruction gain over a static-prefix baseline. On 40 held-out 3D volumes, SonoAtlasWorld achieves liver and macro-organ AFI of 0.428 and 0.262, compared with at most 0.117 and 0.038 for the tested action- and geometry-conditioned methods. Long-rollout alignment reduces brightness drift by 3.46x at the end of 40 repeated scan cycles. SonoAtlasWorld also generates offline policy-training demonstrations and supports anatomically grounded closed-loop evaluation. Scaling the generated training data improves key-plane acquisition success from 48.2% to 81.2% on unseen anatomies in simulation, demonstrating its utility for robotic ultrasound policy learning.
papers.comment: Interactive video demonstrations are available at: https://sonoatlasworld.github.io/SonoAtlasWorld

papers.title: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can improve pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies through imagined experiences. However, existing VLA-MBRL methods primarily rely on large-scale image or video generation world models, incurring large computational overhead. Latent world models offer a more efficient alternative but face two challenges: compounding errors during recursive prediction and incompatibility with VLAs' visual input interfaces. In this work, we propose LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual MBRL framework that leverages latent world models to improve upon pretrained VLAs. LS-MBPO introduces two key techniques: (1) Hierarchical Forcing, which combines dense causal supervision with autoregressive feedback to mitigate compounding prediction errors; and (2) Latent Subchunk Rollouts, which leverage action chunks from a frozen VLA policy and a latent residual policy for successive subchunk refinement, bridging the gap between latent imagination and VLA policy execution. We further introduce a Progress-Conditioned Branch-Start Curriculum that progressively shifts rollout starting points from later to earlier task stages, enabling effective policy learning from short imagined rollouts. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world ALOHA robot show that LS-MBPO achieves superior task performance and training efficiency compared to existing methods.
papers.summary_cn: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can improve pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies through imagined experiences.
